_what_this_is: The first pure Quantum File — a DERIVED semantic record of the physical `main.py`, written under the Quantum CNS mandate (2026-08-08). It contains no executable implementation and replaces nothing: `main.py` stays exactly as it is, and this file is a second view of it. Every entry here is derived from that source and from evidence already in the suite; nothing is inferred from intent, naming, or plausibility. Where evidence is absent the region is named UNPROVEN rather than filled in.
_rules_it_obeys: no executable implementation, no speculative semantics
state spaces, observers, equivalence classes, causal consequences, preconditions, protection evidence, and explicit UNPROVEN regions only
equivalence is always stated relative to a NAMED observation boundary (mandate rule 10)
labels are not deleted for being control-equivalent (mandate rule 8)
no global quotient is claimed (mandate rule 16)

physical_subject.shape_evidence: AST-pinned by tests/characterization/test_main_public_surface.py: imports are EXACTLY {__future__.annotations, cli.app.run_cli}; the only definition is `main`; the tail is `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`.
physical_subject.isolation_evidence: test_no_production_module_imports_from_main: nothing outside tests/ imports from `main`. So `main` has no consumers inside the runtime; its only consumer is the process boundary.

named_states_reachable_through_main.produced_by: cli/app.py:122 (`--version`-class early return), :125, resume replay (cli/resume.py:134 via app.py:147), run_one_shot (cli/one_shot.py, every return is 0), run_repl (cli/repl.py, every return is 0)
cli/app.py:164 (empty --ask), :169 (file-hint preflight failure), and cli/resume.py:101 (invalid trace id) via app.py:147
named_states_reachable_through_main.meaning: the process reports a usage/preflight refusal

main_return_value.states_NOT_produced_here: 1 and every other integer. No return path in the delegate chain yields them. This is an observation about the code as it stands, not a design statement.
main_return_value.argparse_exits_bypass_main_return: `--help` exits 0 and an unknown flag / missing argument / invalid choice exit 2 by raising SystemExit inside argparse, so those codes never pass through `main`'s return at all. Evidence: tests/characterization/test_cli_argparse_surface.py asserts SystemExit codes 0 and 2 directly. Recorded because the process-level state space and `main`'s RETURN state space are not the same set, and conflating them would be the kind of false identity this layer exists to prevent.

process_boundary.evidence: tests/characterization/test_main_public_surface.py::test_the_process_really_exits_with_the_code_main_returned runs a real process with nothing patched and reads the shell's exit code
process_boundary.mutation_on_record: that test's own docstring records the measurement that motivated it: dropping the `return` from `main()` leaves the text guard on the tail green while a failing run exits 0 — a caller gating on the exit code would read an error as success. So the return VALUE has a proven causal consequence at this boundary.

in_process_callers.what_it_reads: the returned int, by calling `main_module.main()` directly
in_process_callers.scope_limitation: this observer patches seams (build_agent, load_dotenv, handle_meta_command). It can observe the value but not the process consequence; only process_boundary proves the latter.

ast_shape_observer.what_it_reads: the source text of main.py — its imports, its single definition, its tail
ast_shape_observer.distinguishes: any edit to the file's shape
ast_shape_observer.class: STRUCTURAL. It fires on any shape change and cannot tell a deliberate edit from a removed contract — recorded as such per the map's protection scale, and NOT counted as behavioural protection.

under_process_boundary.basis: the shell branches on zero versus non-zero; both members of each class are indistinguishable to it because each class has one member here
under_process_boundary.note: this is a partition of the states `main` can RETURN. It is not a partition of process exit codes in general — argparse produces 0 and 2 without passing through the return.

under_main_itself.basis: the body is `return run_cli()`. `main` distinguishes nothing; every distinction visible at the process boundary is produced by the delegate chain and passes through unexamined.
under_main_itself.consequence_for_the_audit: `main` is a PASS-THROUGH, so the semantic content attributed to it belongs to cli/app.py and below. This is why the quantum file for `main` is small and why its interesting regions are all references outward.

causal_consequences_proven.chain: delegate return value -> main return value -> SystemExit argument -> process exit code -> caller's success/failure reading
causal_consequences_proven.evidence: test_the_process_really_exits_with_the_code_main_returned — a real process, nothing patched, using `--file` naming a missing path so the failure happens in preflight and no model is called
causal_consequences_proven.preconditions_proven_by_that_test: the chosen invocation genuinely fails in preflight (exit 2), so the test observes a NON-ZERO code and cannot pass by accident on a run that would have exited 0 anyway

preconditions_recorded.why_they_matter_here: mandate rule 6 — a test that passes because its subject never existed is vacuous. For `main` the subject is a non-zero exit; a test that only ever exercised a successful run could not detect the dropped-return defect at all, which is precisely the failure the process-level test was written to catch.

protection_status.main_return_value_reaches_the_process: PROVEN — behavioural, at the process boundary
protection_status.main_shape: STRUCTURAL only — three AST/text guards; they protect the file's form, not any consequence

unproven_regions.region: the exit-code SEMANTICS of the delegate chain
unproven_regions.statement: That `2` means usage/preflight refusal and `0` means success is read off the call sites, not proven by a test that varies the meaning. No observer distinguishes 'refused because the trace id was invalid' from 'refused because the file hint failed preflight' — both are 2.
unproven_regions.belongs_to: cli/app.py and cli/resume.py — to be walked in their own quantum files, not settled here

unproven_regions.region: whether any caller outside the repository branches on the exit code
unproven_regions.statement: The process-level consequence is proven for a test caller. Whether a CI job, script or supervisor reads it is outside the repository's evidence.
Every observed return in cli/repl.py is 0. Whether a non-zero interactive exit is reachable at all has not been probed.

explicitly_not_claimed: No global quantum count for `main` or for the CLI is asserted.
No equivalence between argparse's exit codes and `main`'s return values is asserted — they are different state spaces that happen to share integers.
No design change is proposed. `main` being a pass-through is an observation, not a complaint.
